chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) inclined [to prostrate], he bowed down while exclaiming Takbir.'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn perform the prostration in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the physical elegance and spiritual mindfulness of Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) during prayer, illustrating the Shia emphasis on *khushu* (humility) through the seamless integration of movement and remembrance. Scholars note that this specific manner of prostration reflects the transition from standing to bowing, serving as a practical model for the *adab* (etiquette) of the body in worship. It underscores the belief that the physical actions of the Imams are not merely ritualistic but carry deep theological significance regarding the connection between the servant and the Divine.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Moalla Abu Usman, from Moalla Bin Khunays,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws while going down for Sajdah, would was exclaim Takbīr’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu‘alla’ abu ‘Uthman from Mu‘alla’ ibn Khunayth who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘
Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, while bowing down for Sajdah (prostration) would say Takbir (Allah is great beyond description).”’ (Ahadith 4-5 are best be explained by fatwa.)
